title: A Multiple Survival Screening algorithm \(MSS) for identifying high-quality cancer prognostic markers
protocol: Generate a survival gene pool in this step by performing a genome-wide single gene survival analysis.
Use several training datasets to obtain multiple survival gene pools for robustness.
Merge these gene pools for further steps.
Generate cancer hallmark related Gene Ontology (GO)-term-defined gene sets from the survival genes using GO analysis tools such as DAVID Bioinformatics Resources.
Ensure each GO-term-defined gene set contains approximately 50~100 genes.
Discard a GO-term-defined gene set if it includes less than 45 genes.
Combine genes to achieve a size between 50 and 100 genes from multiple small GO-term-defined gene sets, if necessary.
For large GO-term-defined gene sets with more than 100 genes, rank the genes and select the top 60-80 genes for further analysis.
Generate 1 million distinct random gene sets from each selected GO-term-defined gene set.
Ensure each random gene set contains 30 genes.
Generate 36 random datasets using the training dataset.
Maintain the same ratio of "good" and "bad" tumors in each RDS as in the original training set.
Include at least 60 samples for each RDS.
Perform survival screenings of the random gene sets on the random datasets.
Set parameters in the MSS algorithm to select predictive RGSs with a survival p-value less than 0.05 in more than 90% of the RDSs.
Consider adjusting parameters if p-values are less than 0.01 and RDS passing rate is between 75% and 95%.
Select several thousand random gene sets using adjusted parameters.
Identify the top 30 most frequent genes as a potential gene signature from the selected RGSs.
Discard the experiment if more than 30% of the 1 million RGSs have p-values less than 0.05 in more than 35 RDSs.
Discard the experiment if only a few hundred RGSs have p-values less than 0.05 in less than 80% of the RDSs.
Consider running more RGSs (4 or 8 million) to obtain sufficient selected RGSs based on datasets and GO-term-defined gene sets.
Obtain a potential gene signature containing the top-ranked 30 most frequent genes from the selected RGSs.
Assess the reproducibility and stability of the potential gene signature by examining common genes between two top-ranked 30 genes derived from two distinct 1 million RGSs on the same RDS set.
Evaluate the performance of the selected gene signatures in independent testing datasets, ensuring they have survival p-values less than 0.05 if the MSS protocol is followed.
